environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; raw socket client and strict upstream peer

findings.description: close is computed as ++c.count>=loc->s.keepreq where c.count lives on the Client and the limit comes from whichever location this request resolved to. Visiting /one/ (keepalive_requests 1) and then a /two/ request on the same connection still sees count reach the low limit and closes, and vice versa a high-limit location lets the counter run past a sibling's configured limit. One request is enough to observe: after the counter meets the low limit the response carries Connection: close. Precondition: two locations with different keepalive_requests.
findings.title: keepalive_requests is compared against a counter shared by every location on the connection, so a low-limit location closes the connection for a different one

findings.description: apply() stores keepalive_timeout into s.keepsec and the close expression consults it only through !loc->s.keepsec (zero vs non-zero), never as a duration. The enforced idle deadline is the literal if(time(nullptr)-c.last>75) in the poll loop, so a configured keepalive_timeout 2s still leaves the socket alive for 75s and a configured large value does not extend past 75s. Precondition: none beyond a keepalive connection.
findings.title: keepalive_timeout is parsed into keepsec and never read; the real idle deadline is a hardcoded 75 seconds

findings.description: The close decision is taken before the pipelined tail is processed, and the processed tail is only re-run after the write completes and only when close is false. Sending two requests in one packet where the first hits a keepalive_requests 1 location returns only the first response; the second is dropped with no error to the client. Precondition: a low keepalive_requests location and a pipelined packet.
findings.title: A pipelined second request is eaten when the first response closes the connection

limitations: All RCE is on the upstream host
Needs a proxied location that sets a low keepalive_requests
The build dials a fresh upstream per request, so no pool poisoning here
